claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The source frames intent-centric human-agent work as shaped by natural language, repository context, tools, tests, and governance.
claims.quote: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and agentic systems are moving software engineering from code-centric production toward intent-centric human-agent work in which natural language, repository context, tools, tests, and governance shape delivery.

claims.question: q3

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The findings describe software engineering as shifting from isolated code authorship toward supervising, validating, and governing socio-technical systems of humans, agents, tools, and evidence gates.
claims.quote: The findings indicate that software engineering is becoming less about isolated code authorship and more about supervising, validating, and governing socio-technical systems of humans, agents, tools, and evidence gates.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The study bases its claims on reflexive thematic analysis and IPA-informed public-discourse/document analysis of peer-reviewed literature, benchmarks, talks, interviews, essays, announcements, and X-originated discourse.
claims.quote: This study addresses that gap through a reflexive thematic analysis (RTA) dominant and interpretative phenomenological analysis (IPA) informed public-discourse and document analysis. claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The source warns that speed-focused adoption can accumulate hidden technical debt and accountability gaps, while bounded autonomy can preserve quality, security, maintainability, and trust.
claims.quote: This matters because speed-focused adoption can accumulate hidden technical debt and accountability gaps, whereas bounded autonomy can preserve quality, security, maintainability, and trust.
